newsitem.title: ESTONIA: DRAFT EXCISE LAW TO AFFECT SAKU - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: DRAFT EXCISE LAW TO AFFECT SAKU - REPORT.

text.p: A new draft excise law before the Riigikogu (parliament) threatens to favour Tartu brewery over Saku brewery in the collection of excise duties based on beer production, Aripaev business daily said on Wednesday.
Tartu is part-owned by Finnish Olvi while Saku is owned by Baltic Beverages, itself owned by Hartwall and Pripps.
The draft law would mean that market leader Saku would pay more in excise tax than rival Tartu, because Saku's production is over 20 million litres, the paper said.
The newspaper quoted Tartu's general manager Madis Paddar as sayign that the tax treatment of Saku and Tartu should be different.
Saku holds 55 percent of the local beer market and Tartu has a 19 percent market share, the paper added.
